items.titleEn: Nvidia stock faces a new Jensen Huang crisis as Elon Musk enters the fight
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. The stock is being hit by leadership/governance noise, but the core AI demand and Nvidia’s product position haven’t changed. Tuesday’s key is whether data-center revenue and gross margin (guided ~74%) hold and whether guidance stays intact; a credible interim-to-permanent succession plan plus stable export-control messaging should trigger a fast re-rating. The Musk petition is also a near-term catalyst for “board credibility” headlines that can calm investors. Key Risk: A guidance miss or margin compression tied to customer delays or export-control restrictions that directly hit future chip sales. Buy ARM. The article flags Nvidia’s board exploring Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential role, which signals governance/leadership reshuffling risk is being actively managed. If Nvidia stabilizes, Arm benefits indirectly via continued AI compute platform momentum and reduced “AI supply chain disruption” fears. Even without a direct deal, the market often rerates Arm when major AI chip ecosystems look less likely to stall.

items.titleEn: Why are Samsung, SK Hynix stocks falling sharply ahead of Nvidia earnings?
items.summaryEn: Buy Samsung Electronics. It’s broader than pure-memory (semiconductors + phones/other), so it’s less likely to be crushed by a single AI-memory demand wobble. If Nvidia’s results are merely “okay” rather than bad, Samsung’s diversified earnings base should hold up better than SK Hynix and the market may rotate back toward the more resilient name. Key Risk: A broad risk-off move hits Korean tech and Samsung’s semiconductor segment also guides to weaker margins or weaker memory pricing, making diversification irrelevant. Sell SK Hynix. The stock is the most exposed to premium AI memory demand, and the article flags “cliff in earnings” risk in 2028 plus possible data-center delays if Nvidia’s AI spending outlook disappoints. Even with record profits, the market is trading uncertainty around future margins, not current results.
